newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top Germans see 3.2 million jobless in 2000 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Top Germans see 3.2 million jobless in 2000 - survey.

text.p: Leading representatives from politics, the media, industry and associations in Germany believe unemployment could fall to 3.2 million in 2000, a German survey showed on Tuesday.

A majority of those surveyed by German public relations agency Kohtes und Klewes and German Emnid research institute said they did not expect Chancellor Helmut Kohl to fulfil his goal of halving unemployment currently at 4.5 million by 2000.
But parliamentarians were more optimistic than representatives from industry and lobby groups about the government's chances of achieving its ambitious aim.

The survey was conducted in April among 61 German parliamentarians, 86 top government officials, 78 senior editors and 53 leading representatives from industry and associations. The survey is carried three times a year.
Forty-five percent of all those polled said the most pressing problem on the government's hands was the need to reduce the tax burden on companies in order to create jobs.

The creation of jobs was regarded by 71 percent as the biggest challenge for the economy and 52 percent said promotion of technology and investment in research presented an antidote to the weaknesses of the German economy.
